newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Woosung creditors, Hanil agree on takeover scheme.
newsitem.headline: Woosung creditors, Hanil agree on takeover scheme.

text.p: Hanil Group said on Saturday it has agreed on a scheme with creditors of Woosung Construction Co to takeover the debt-ridden company.
Hanil Group's spokesman said Hanil Synthetic Fiber Co and Kukje Corp would be the group's main affiliates to aquire Woosung shares in May.
In return, Hanil will raise 274.6 billion won by selling off real estate and borrow 275.7 billion won from Woosung creditors for operation funds for the construction company, the spokesman said.

Korea First Bank, Woosung's main creditor, said the 18-year redemption plan for 275.7 billion won fixed bank interest rates at 3.5 percent for the first six years, prime rate for the six years to follow and prime plus five percentage points for the last six years.

The bank's spokesman added that interest rates for non-banking institutes were fixed at 6.815 percent the first six years and 1.685 percent points less than Korea First Bank's prime rate for the remaining 12 years.

Hanil was chosen last May to take over Woosung, which defaulted on promissory notes worth 16.9 billion won in January 1996. Woosung Construction was South Korea's third largest home builder and the 18th largest construction company.
